Let \(q\ge1\), let \(p_\star\) be a positive density, and let \(\{S_l\}_{l=1}^K\) be measurable supports whose probability under \(p_\star\) is at most \(C_0w^q\), with uniformly bounded overlap and an intersection graph of uniformly bounded degree. Let \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_K\) be independent Rademacher signs. Suppose two positive density families have the same one-observation mixture \(p_\star\), give every \(S_l\) the same probability as \(p_\star\), and, after division by \(p_\star\), can be written as
\[
 \frac{p_\lambda}{p_\star}=1+A_\lambda,
 \qquad
 \frac{q_\lambda}{p_\star}=1+A_\lambda+B_\lambda+C_\lambda,
\]
where \(A_\lambda\) is linear in the signs with local coefficients bounded by \(R\), \(B_\lambda\) is linear with local coefficients bounded by \(D\le R\), and \(C_\lambda\) is a centered quadratic Rademacher polynomial with coefficients bounded by \(DR\), each coefficient being supported on the corresponding support or support intersection. Assume every density ratio obtained by adding an arbitrary subset of the residual terms is bounded above and below by fixed positive constants and preserves the support probabilities. If \(Nw^qR^2\le c_0\), then
\[
 \operatorname{TV}^2\!\left(\mathbb E_\lambda P_\lambda^{\otimes N},
 \mathbb E_\lambda Q_\lambda^{\otimes N}\right)
 \le C N^2K w^{2q}(D^2R^2+D^4),
\]
where \(c_0>0\) is sufficiently small and \(C<\infty\) depends only on the ratio, overlap, and support constants.

For every fixed calibrated \(\kappa\), every \(\gamma>d\), and all sufficiently large \(n\), there are constants \(0<c_1\le C_1<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that
\[
 c_1 n^{-2\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
 \le \mathfrak R_n(1,\gamma;\kappa)
 \le C_1 n^{-2\min\{\beta,\gamma\}/\{2\min\{\beta,\gamma\}+d\}}.
\]
If \(\beta\ge\gamma\), then the high-smoothness branch of \(r_n^*\) applies and
\[
 \mathfrak R_n(1,\gamma;\kappa)\asymp(r_n^*)^2.
\]
If \(\beta<\gamma\), the two displayed powers are strictly different. In the high-smoothness branch the lower endpoint equals \((r_n^*)^2\), but the available upper endpoint is strictly slower. Every point in the low-smoothness branch has \(\beta<\gamma\); writing \(T=1+d/(4\bar s)+d/(2\gamma)\), its three exponents satisfy
\[
 \frac{2\beta}{2\beta+d}<\frac{2}{T}<\frac{2\gamma}{2\gamma+d}.
\]
Thus the frozen bounds settle the subregime \(\beta\ge\gamma\), while exactness remains unresolved for \(\beta<\gamma\), including the entire low-smoothness branch.
